page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-56 is a compute-optimized virtual machine tailored for compute-intensive tasks requiring high core counts. Powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor family, the instance provisions 56 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 28 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 112 GB, reflecting a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU). The architecture features a 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware support for AES, VAES, SHA-NI cryptographic extensions, and standard AVX vector execution, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets.

Benchmark results show top-quartile results across parallelized compute metrics, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 82,135.96 and a PassMark CPU score of 63,273.31. Multi-threaded software compilation in Clang (41,115.0) and ray tracing (60,928.0) demonstrate efficient scaling across all 56 virtual cores. Memory subsystem testing reflects top-tier cached throughput at 3,817.65 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidth stabilize at 138.2 GB/sec and 69.21 GB/sec, respectively. Single-core performance falls within median tiers, confirming the architecture is heavily biased toward aggregate parallel throughput rather than raw single-thread speed.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating remote persistent disks for filesystem operations. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. From a resource-efficiency standpoint, the 2 GB per core ratio ensures organizations avoid paying for excess idle memory when running strictly compute-bound jobs. Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-56 is appropriately matched for CI/CD build pipelines, distributed batch processing, video rendering, scientific modeling, and parallel transcoding workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-56 is a compute-optimized instance engineered for parallel processing workloads. Based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 architecture, it features 56 dedicated vCPUs across 28 physical cores and 112 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server includes hardware-level cryptography accelerators such as AES and SHA-NI, but excludes AVX-512 extensions, local storage, and dedicated GPUs. Performance testing highlights strong multi-core scalability, achieving top-quartile marks in multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks, paired with top-tier cached memory metrics. The lack of local NVMe storage requires external persistent storage attachments. By prioritizing CPU density over extensive memory footprints, this instance delivers strong compute efficiency for workloads such as large software builds, media encoding, distributed analytics, and batch processing.
